balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

customerConcentration.title: Largest customer concentration
customerConcentration.content:
The percentage of revenue from Skyworks' single largest customer, disclosed annually in the 10-K. Interim periods are not separately disclosed, so this chart is FY-only.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: that customer is Apple. Concentration rose from 58% in FY2022 to a peak of 69% in FY2024 as Skyworks' non-Apple business shrank faster than its Apple content, then eased to 61% in FY2026 as the Qorvo merger adds a more diversified revenue base (defense, infrastructure, Android RF).

What to watch:

  • Whether the post-merger entity's concentration keeps falling or Apple content simply gets added to a bigger base
  • Any signal from Apple on in-house RF development, which is the tail risk this number proxies for

rdIntensity.title: R&D spending and intensity
rdIntensity.content:
R&D expense in dollars against R&D as a percentage of revenue, both annual-only (the geographic/customer 10-K disclosures are not broken out quarterly).

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: R&D intensity nearly doubled from 11.3% of revenue in FY2022 to 21.1% in FY2026 -- not because spending accelerated much in dollar terms, but because revenue fell from a cyclical RF downturn while R&D held up. That combination (flat-to-rising R&D cost, falling sales) is the margin-pressure signal behind the period.

What to watch:

  • Whether R&D intensity normalizes as revenue recovers and post-merger overlap is cut, or stays structurally higher
  • Qorvo integration: the DCF's SBC and R&D lines are already pro forma combined, so this chart's FY2026 point is Skyworks standalone, not the merged base the valuation uses

revenueGeo.title: Revenue by geography
revenueGeo.content:
Revenue split by end-market geography, as disclosed in the 10-K/10-Q.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: "US" and "China" are shipment destinations for chips that mostly end up in phones assembled in China and sold worldwide, not end-customer geography -- the US bucket is large because that is where Apple's contract manufacturing relationship is booked, not because end demand is domestic. Every region outside the US has shrunk since FY2022 as the smartphone RF cycle turned down.

What to watch:

  • Whether non-US, non-Apple regions (broad-markets diversification) start growing again post-merger
  • Don't read this as true geographic end-demand exposure

revenueChannel.title: Revenue by channel
revenueChannel.content:
Distributor revenue is sold through third-party distributors (mostly serving the broad-markets/IoT business); direct revenue is sold straight to large OEMs.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: direct revenue is overwhelmingly Apple and a handful of other large handset OEMs, so this split is a second lens on customer concentration -- it fell from $4.49bn distributor / $1.0bn direct in FY2022 to $3.39bn / $0.57bn in FY2026, both channels shrinking with the cycle.

What to watch:

  • Direct channel revenue as a cross-check on the Apple concentration chart
  • Distributor sell-through trends as the earlier signal of broad-markets demand turning

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Skyworks Solutions, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
